Onerous

/OH-nuh-ruhs/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Onerous means burdensome; involving a heavy, oppressive amount of effort or obligation

Onerous means burdensome; involving a heavy, oppressive amount of effort or obligation. The lease came with onerous conditions, including weekly inspections and a security deposit worth three months' rent.

Worked Example

Counting the warehouse's entire inventory by hand fell to Priya's crew, an onerous assignment that kept them scanning shelves through three straight overnight shifts.

The assignment demands an enormous, exhausting amount of effort that weighs heavily on the crew for nights on end. A duty that presses down on people like a heavy load is exactly what onerous describes.

How Onerous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

burdensome

burdensome: causing a heavy load of work or worry

taxing

Antonyms

effortless

effortless: requiring no work at all

light

light: easy to bear or carry out

How Strong Is It? — demanding → onerous → crushing

demanding vs. onerous

demanding vs. onerous: A demanding job asks a lot of you; an onerous one weighs on you like a heavy burden you can barely carry.

crushing vs. onerous

crushing vs. onerous: A crushing workload goes beyond onerous, so overwhelming that it flattens any hope of keeping up.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — oner

Root — oner: burden, load (Latin onus, oneris)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of, possessing

Put it together

Put it together: The Latin root oner comes from onus, meaning 'burden,' and the suffix -ous means 'full of.' An onerous duty is literally one 'full of burden,' a load that presses down on whoever must carry it.

Use the root in a new word: onus

Use the root in a new word: onus: The onus, or burden of proof, is on the borrower to show that the loan was repaid.

Root Check

Word Choice

Formal / legal

Onerous appears often in formal and legal contexts, in collocations like onerous duties, onerous obligations, and onerous terms of a contract. Distinguish it from arduous, which stresses the strenuous physical effort a task takes; onerous stresses the oppressive weight of a duty or obligation on the person stuck with it.
